title: Keeping in touch: newsletters and a consent-based contact plan
audience: Owners and staff who send newsletters, texts or emails to clients and prospects
learningOutcomes: Explain the consent, sender identification and unsubscribe requirements for commercial electronic messages in Australia
Build a contact cadence that mixes a regular newsletter with personal touches
Keep a consent record and action each opt-out within five business days

instruction.heading: Why steady contact matters
instruction.body: People cannot refer you if they have forgotten you. A regular newsletter keeps the business visible without constant selling. The content is what earns attention: training tips checked for accuracy, schedule changes, a member story used with permission, and a clear next step. Keep the tone plain and the frequency predictable, so readers know what to expect.

instruction.heading: Consent comes first
instruction.body: Under the Spam Act 2003, a commercial electronic message needs the recipient's consent. Consent may be express, given knowingly, or in limited cases inferred from an ongoing relationship. Each message must identify the sender accurately, with correct contact details, and must carry an unsubscribe option that is clear, free and easy to use. The ACMA guidance checked on 2026-11-02 says opt-out requests must be acted on within five business days. A purchased list does not transfer responsibility for consent.

instruction.heading: Plan the cadence with personal touches
instruction.body: A monthly newsletter works well alongside a handful of personal touches, for example a note of thanks after a milestone, a birthday card, or a check-in after a long absence. Record each touch with its date, so you can see whether the plan is too heavy or too light. Stop any touch when the person asks you to stop.

procedure: List each contact source and the evidence of consent for each contact.
Remove from electronic lists any contact without a consent record. Keep a contact only where a lawful basis is confirmed.
Write a newsletter template with the sender's identity, contact details and a working unsubscribe.
Set a fixed monthly newsletter date and a short list of personal touches.
Action each opt-out within five business days and record the date.

workedExamples.situation: A hypothetical yoga studio has 120 contacts: 70 joined through a sign-up form that said they would receive updates, 30 were passed on by referral with no consent record, and 20 came from a bought list.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: Which contacts may receive electronic newsletters, and what happens to the rest?
workedExamples.reasoning: The 70 with a sign-up record may receive messages, subject to the sender and unsubscribe rules. The 30 referred contacts have no consent record and should not receive electronic marketing until consent is obtained. The 20 from the bought list cannot be relied on as consent and come off electronic marketing lists.

equipmentAndPpe: Consent record: sign-up form showing date and source
Newsletter template with sender details and unsubscribe

commonErrors.error: Emailing a purchased or scraped list
commonErrors.prevention: Use only contacts with a consent record.

commonErrors.error: An unsubscribe link that asks for a login or extra details
commonErrors.prevention: Make opt-out a single step that asks for no extra information.

commonErrors.error: Leaving out the sender's name and contact details
commonErrors.prevention: Put the business name, ABN and a working contact on every message, as the template requires.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Spam Act 2003: consent, sender identification and unsubscribe for commercial electronic messages. Spam Act 2003 summary, ACMA https://www.acma.gov.au/avoid-sending-spam, checked 2026-11-02. This is a summary, not legal advice.
Check current Privacy Act 1988 obligations before storing new contact fields.
Check carrier or provider terms before sending texts.

qualityStandard: Every electronic contact has a dated consent record
Every message shows sender identity and a working unsubscribe
Every opt-out is actioned within five business days and recorded
documentationEvidence: Consent register showing source, date and method
summary: Consent first: no record, no electronic marketing.
Action opt-outs within five business days.

knowledgeChecks.question: Under the Spam Act guidance in this lesson, a commercial electronic message must include:
options: A sender identity and a working unsubscribe option
A discount code and a link to the price list, sent each Friday

knowledgeChecks.question: Opt-out requests should be actioned within:
A purchased mailing list means:
options: Consent is covered for every address on it by the list seller
The business is still responsible for confirming consent
No records need to be kept once the mail has been sent

knowledgeChecks.question: Which personal touch does the lesson give as an example?
options: A note of thanks after a milestone

officialReferences.title: Avoid sending spam
officialReferences.covers: ACMA guidance on the Spam Act 2003: consent is required before marketing messages, and keeping a record of express consent is advised; inferred consent is less reliable than express consent; the sender must be identified accurately with correct contact details kept for at least 30 days; every commercial message must contain an unsubscribe option that is clear, free, needs no account or extra personal information, and works for at least 30 days; unsubscribe requests must be honoured within 5 working days. Publisher: Australian Communications and Media Authority (ACMA). This is a summary of the guidance, not the Act text, which was not read.
